puppet_equipment_record.name: coiler
puppet_equipment_record.element_slot_interpretation: Thunder element capacity cost 2 (0x20000 nibble encoding)

conditional_interactions.reason: Coiler modifier row has opticFiber=true; performance boost changes modifier magnitude when compatible Optic Fiber effects are active.
getManeuverCount treats active maneuvers under Overdrive as three for attachment modifier scaling.

required_dependency_classes.description: Internal item_puppet attachment identity, slot type, element-slot cost, and attachment index.
Mapping between obtainable inventory item/sub-ID semantics and internal puppet-equipment identity.
Shared automaton attachment modifier engine and Coiler modifier row.
DOUBLE_ATTACK modifier definition and compatible target semantics.
CItemPuppet equip slot/element-slot representation and item loading.
Puppet unlock/equip/update/maneuver hooks and dynamic Lua dispatch.
char_pet attachment unlock/equip persistence used by puppetutils.
Automaton WS scripts using getExtraHits so Coiler affects multi-hit behavior correctly.
Shop/drop paths that make Coiler obtainable; package reviewer may include/exclude acquisition separately from behavior.
Optic Fiber and Overdrive/maneuver interactions that modify Coiler behavior but are not hard prerequisites.

known_current_toolkit_gaps: No item_puppet logical table/profile exists in current server adapters.
No canonical mapping exists between obtainable inventory item identity and internal puppet attachment identity/sub-ID semantics.
Dynamic C++ Lua dispatch by attachment name is not guaranteed to produce item_puppet -> attachment Lua artifact edges.

Shared automaton.lua contains behavior for many attachments, so package scope needs symbol/section-level dependency evidence without automatically treating every attachment in the file as a Coiler dependency.
Modifier semantics such as DOUBLE_ATTACK are not currently modeled as a complete Lua -> enum -> core behavior dependency chain for package closure.
Coiler weapon-skill fan-out through xi.automaton.getExtraHits is not currently guaranteed to be discovered transitively.
Persistence dependencies on char_pet.unlocked_attachments/equipped_attachments are not currently represented as schema dependencies.
Conditional interactions such as Optic Fiber amplification need a relationship distinct from hard REQUIRES.
Acquisition paths (shop/drop) need reviewer-controlled scope separate from the attachment behavior implementation.
Current package discovery has no Automaton/Puppet domain analyzer to seed these logical relationships.
